Figure 8:Input-dependent frequency partitions learned by DBS-BSRNN on DnR v2.
Each row corresponds to one test mixture and shows the hard
boundaries predicted for its central three-second window. Mixture order
is shared by all panels. Boundary locations varied most strongly in B4,
whereas B2 retained a comparatively stable layout.

Figure 10:Predicted boundaries across seven overlapping windows of one DnR v2 test
mixture. Each row is a separate 3-second inference window and adjacent
windows had a 1.5-second hop. The example had the median mean temporal
replacement rate among the 64 analyzed mixtures. The partition was fixed
within each window and changed between windows.
